historical.message:
fix(site): upgrade astro 5->7 to clear dependabot alerts

Bump astro 5.18.2 -> 7.1.3, clearing all 9 open dependabot alerts on
the marketing site (8 astro XSS/SSRF advisories + 1 esbuild dev-server
file-read). Astro 7 pulled a vulnerable sharp <0.35.0 (libvips CVEs);
npm audit fix bumped it. npm audit now reports 0 vulnerabilities.

Practical exposure of the original alerts was near-nil: static output,
no SSR adapter, no user input, esbuild dev-only. This is hygiene to
close the alerts. Verified: astro build exit 0, all 3 pages generated.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow
Not-tested: no visual/browser check; static build output only

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(scan): dedupe hotkey hints and equalize control sizes

Strip the (R)/(K) parentheticals from the Rescan and Recalibrate buttons
now that the always-on legend already lists those keys; hover tooltips
still name them. Drop the dynamic degree suffix from the Rotate label
(the is-active state and aria-label already convey rotation). Give the
shared camera-control spec a uniform min-width so the toolbar controls
render the same size.

Constraint: legend remains the single visible keybinding reference; tooltips keep the keys discoverable on hover.
Rejected: removing keys from the legend instead of the buttons (legend was the agreed always-on shortcut surface).
Directive: no duplicate keybindings, make the controls all the same size.
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow
Not-tested: no automated coverage of button labels or control widths (none pre-existed); tsc and biome pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: gate map pin drag behind explicit adjust mode

Stop pins on the trip map were draggable at all times (mouse and keyboard
arrows), so panning the map often nudged a pin by accident. Dragging is now
locked behind a deliberate per-stop action: tap a pin to open its editor,
click "Adjust location on map" to unlock that one pin (with a ring
affordance), then "Done adjusting" / closing the editor / selecting another
stop re-locks it. Read-only maps (share, print, marketing demo) stay
non-draggable, unchanged.

Adjust state lives in useEditingStopLifecycle (adjustingStopId), auto-clears
on any selection change. TripMap creates markers non-draggable and an effect
toggles setDraggable + the affordance for the active stop; keyboardDrag gains
an isEnabled gate that keeps Escape/blur flush reachable so a pending write is
never stranded. Persistence path (onMarkerDrag -> autosave -> Convex) is
unchanged.

Constraint: no else statements, why-only comments, no read-only regression.
Rejected: a global map-wide edit-mode toggle (too coarse; user asked for a
per-stop action).
Directive: lock pin drag behind a deliberate action per user request.
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: moderate
Not-tested: live browser drag; covered by astro check, biome, keyboardDrag
unit tests, and StopCardEditor/rail browser tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(theme): add Rainbow Unicorns pastel light theme

Add a fifth theme, unicorn ("Rainbow Unicorns (Pastel)"), to the THEMES

All accent, state, and muted-text colors verified at or above 4.5:1 WCAG

draft values.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow
Not-tested: visual appearance in a live browser session

feat(detail): replace copies list with count badge and enlarge card image

The per-copy list in the card detail panel (location, status, copy number)
provided no value in this view; the copy count is now a chip badge next to
the condition/printing chips, with a skeleton chip while the detail IPC
call loads. The panel widens from 440px to 560px (380px to 480px under the

aspect-ratio so the no-image placeholder keeps a card-shaped box.

Removes the now-unused highlightPhysicalCardId prop and its SearchTab call

Constraint: CardStatusText and LocationCode components kept; still used by
StorageTab, PlacementStage, and guided picking.
Rejected: showing the count in the provenance footer; the chips row keeps
it visible next to the other card attributes.
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow
Not-tested: no component tests exist for this panel (logic-only test
convention); verified via tsc and biome only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(search): paginate storage:search with server-side limit

storage:search now takes optional limit/offset with a server default of
200 and a hard clamp of 500, so no caller can fetch unbounded results.
Response adds totalCount (COUNT sharing the row query's joins and
filters) and hasMore; explicit ORDER BY physicalCards.id makes pages
deterministic. SearchTab accumulates pages behind a Load more button
with a mono "Showing X of Y" count line, resets on any filter change,
guards races via request ids plus a committed-query snapshot, and moves
focus to the count line when the last page arrives. Guided Picking's
name lookup shows an inline notice when results are capped instead of
silently truncating. Five db tests cover hasMore boundaries, clamping,
and offset walks with no overlap.

Constraint: db suite must run via the Electron-hosted vitest invocation; plain node vitest hits the known better-sqlite3 ABI mismatch in this worktree.
Rejected: infinite scroll; explicit Load more keeps keyboard flow and row focus predictable for the card detail panel.
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow
Not-tested: renderer pagination UI has no unit tests; verified via typecheck, lint, 123/123 db tests, and two review passes.

New card:detail IPC channel returns card attributes from the newest scan
row, market price with scan fallback, the latest TCGplayer pricing

Confidence: high

Not-tested: no unit test infra for renderer; verified via typecheck, biome lint, and two reviewer passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(brand): standardize logo across site and social onto one mark The Card Harbor logo had diverged: the app/taskbar icon and og-image used the detailed harbor mark, while the site favicon and the inline header SVGs used a different, simplified redraw. Unify everything onto the single brand mark (src/renderer/src/assets/card-harbor-mark.png) that the app icon already uses. - generate-icon.mjs: promote from app-icon-only to the single source for every logo raster. In addition to build/icon.{ico,png} it now emits the full site favicon set (favicon.ico, favicon-16x16, favicon-32x32, apple-touch-icon, a favicon.svg badge), a square logo.png for schema.org Organization.logo, and a square, transparent brand-mark.png for in-page headers. brand-mark.png is padded to a square canvas so a fixed square CSS box renders it without distortion. - generate-og-image.mjs (new): rebuilds site/public/og-image.png from the same mark, de-shadowing it for the white card. Centered lockup (mark + one-line name + tagline) survives a square center-crop so Slack/Discord/ iMessage thumbnails stay readable. - Base.astro: wire the full favicon set + web manifest + theme-color, and point Organization.logo at /logo.png (square raster) instead of the SVG. - index.astro, Legal.astro: replace the inline simplified brand-mark SVG in the header with so headers use the real mark. - site.webmanifest (new): PWA manifest referencing the generated icons. Constraint: keep one brand mark as the single source; the app icon already uses it, so the site and social assets move to it rather than the reverse. Rejected: keeping a separate simplified favicon/header glyph (the whole point was that it read as a different logo); vectorizing the raster mark (it is a raster brand asset, so favicon.svg wraps it and og/headers use PNGs). Directive: standardize the logo, seeing different versions across app, site, and SEO. Confidence: high Scope-risk: narrow Not-tested: no automated coverage; verified by running both generators, building the site (6 pages), inspecting the built head for the favicon set / manifest / theme-color / JSON-LD logo, and eyeballing the mark at favicon, header (28px, undistorted), and og-image sizes plus a 240px square crop. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context)

fix(session): tear down worktree after PTY reap on quick delete

Quick delete fired sess.discardWorktree() unawaited and BEFORE
sess.destroy() killed the PTY. On Windows `git worktree remove --force`
fails while the live claude/conhost process still holds the worktree as
its cwd (directory lock); the swallowed failure leaked the worktree, and
the follow-up `branch -D` then failed too (branch still checked out), so
a same-named re-add hit "session branch already checked out; running in
place". Destroy first, then discard only after the _killReap promise
settles, so removal runs on a dead process and drops both worktree and
branch cleanly.

Constraint: _teardownSession stays sync (called from a sync reload loop); discard is deferred fire-and-forget, ordered via the reap promise.
Rejected: awaiting discard inline (would make teardown async across all callers); killing PTY inside discardWorktree (couples an operator action to the teardown path).
Directive: Explicit removal throws the worktree away; shutdown/restart still skip discard so pending-review worktrees survive the next-boot reconcile.
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow
Not-tested: live Windows quick-delete + same-name re-add (verified by root-cause reasoning + existing teardown/kill suites, 50 pass)

historical.message:
feat(site): add SEO metadata, structured data, and crawl files

Harden the marketing site for search and social sharing. Add self-referencing
canonical, full Open Graph + Twitter summary_large_image tags, and a generated
1200x630 og-image.png so links unfurl with a real preview card. Emit JSON-LD
for Organization and WebSite sitewide and SoftwareApplication (Free/Pro offers)
on the homepage. Ship robots.txt, sitemap.xml, llms.txt, and Netlify security
headers. Trim the homepage title/description to SERP limits and point internal
legal links at their trailing-slash canonical form to drop a 301 hop.

The Pro offer models the recurring price via UnitPriceSpecification (monthly),
not a flat amount, to match on-page pricing and avoid a rich-results mismatch.
Organization logo points at the square favicon, not the wide social banner.

Constraint: Netlify deploys from main; static Astro; Paddle checkout runs
client-side and must not break.
Rejected: shipping a live Content-Security-Policy (staged commented-out in
_headers to avoid blocking the Paddle checkout iframe/XHR until verified against
a real checkout); @astrojs/sitemap (peer-dep risk vs astro ^7) in favor of a
static sitemap.
Directive: fix upstream, no bandaids; deslop + code-review gates run pre-commit.
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow
Not-tested: live social-unfurl rendering (Facebook Sharing Debugger, LinkedIn
Post Inspector, X/Slack/iMessage paste) requires the deployed URL; CSP remains
disabled pending a live Paddle checkout test.
